source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of comparison operators (PDF 38-39).

blocks.text: Comparison operators do values ya expressions ka muqabla (comparison) karte hain: barabar hain ya nahi, kaun bara hai, kaun chhota waghera. Yeh hamesha boolean value deta hai, yani True ya False. Neeche ka program saare comparison operators istemal karta hai.

# Define variables
x, y = 10, 5
# Greater than
print(x, ">", y, "=", x > y)  # Output: 10 > 5 = True
# Less than
print(x, "<", y, "=", x < y)  # Output: 10 < 5 = False
# Equal to
print(x, "==", y, "=", x == y)  # Output: 10 == 5 = False
# Not equal to
print(x, "!=", y, "=", x != y)  # Output: 10 != 5 = True
# Greater than or equal to
print(x, ">=", y, "=", x >= y)  # Output: 10 >= 5 = True
# Less than or equal to
print(x, "<=", y, "=", x <= y)  # Output: 10 <= 5 = False
Is code mein do variables x = 10 aur y = 5 bana kar un ka muqabla >, <, ==, !=, >= aur <= se kiya gaya hai. Har line ka asal output wahi hai jo comment mein likha hai, maslan "10 > 5 = True".

items: == barabar (equal to), != barabar nahi (not equal to)
>= bara ya barabar, <= chhota ya barabar

blocks.explanation: = variable ko qeemat deta hai (x = 10); == do qeematon ka muwazna kar ke True ya False deta hai (x == 10).

items: Comparison operators: > < == != >= <=; nateeja True ya False.
= value deta hai, == muqabla karta hai.
